subject: Private sync gap during v2.3.1 upgrade — ops checkpoint
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medicor.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed private sync gap during your v2.3.1 upgrade

Sanjay —

I wanted to flag that during the v2.3.1 upgrade window this morning we observed a brief synchronization gap between the private control plane and the customer agent fleet in your staging VPC. Symptoms we saw: several API requests returned 503 for ~2s, and agent heartbeats experienced a short lapse which caused the management-plane to reassign a small set of handlers.

What we’ve done so far:
- Immediate roll-forward of a configuration toggle to increase control-plane heartbeat window (temporary mitigation).
- Collected detailed heartbeat logs and KV sync traces for the affected nodes (attached).
- Opened JIRA-PRIV-4567 to track root cause and timeline.

We do not believe customer data was affected; traffic resumed normal servicing within the mitigation window. That said, I want to set expectations: we will do a deeper RCA, surface any config drift, and propose a durable fix.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick bridge to walk through timeline and artifacts — I’m available 11:00–12:30 PT today.
2) Internal RCA + configuration diff within 24 hours.
3) Formal postmortem and runbook update within 72 hours.

Attaching the heartbeat logs and a config diff snapshot for your review.

Thanks and sorry for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a clear timeline.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: privnet-heartbeat-logs-20280514.zip, controlplane-config-diff-20280514.txt

Subject: Internal: quick RCA and bridge scheduling — MediCor private sync gap

Ben / Marcus / Grace —

Looping you in: MediCor experienced a short control-plane sync gap during their v2.3.1 private upgrade window. Customer-facing notes are above.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: can you look at the controlplane logs and agent KV store traces and confirm whether this is a timing regression introduced by the v2.3.1 upgrade or an out-of-band config drift? Please prioritize — they want an initial RCA for their audit.
- Ben: FYI for leadership / credit discussions if the RCA shows we should offer a service credit.
- Grace: please coordinate the bridge at 11:15 PT and keep the customer updated.

Bridge details: I’ll join, Marcus please be ready to share logs and a one-slide timeline.

Thanks —
Tessa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medicor.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 14:20:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed private sync gap during your v2.3.1 upgrade — preliminary findings

All —

We completed an initial sweep of the logs and the attached artifacts show two correlated items: a short-lived leader re-election triggered by an edge-case sequence in the new v2.3.1 controlplane reconcilers, and a config parameter on the customer cluster which had a tighter heartbeat timeout than our recommended baseline (their control-plane heartbeat window was reduced to 1.5s vs our recommended 3s). The combination created a tight race during the upgrade when some agents briefly missed the heartbeat and were reassigned.

What this means:
- Root cause: timing regression in the v2.3.1 reconciler + customer-side heartbeat setting outside recommended baseline.
- Scope: ~12 agent instances in the staging VPC (IDs listed in controlplane-config-diff-20280514.txt).
- Data impact: none detected — KV syncs were eventually consistent and no tokens were lost.

Actions completed:
- We reverted the reconciler toggle that introduced the faster leader handoff (temporary fix).
- We provided MediCor with a recommended heartbeat baseline and configuration hardening checklist.
- JIRA-PRIV-4567 updated with the timeline and artifacts (logs attached).

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Marcus: push a guarded fix to the reconciler code path and run the canary (ETA 7 days).
- Tessa / Grace: coordinate a follow-up upgrade window with MediCor once we validate the guarded fix (ETA contact within 48 hours).
- Ben: estimate expected credit exposure if needed (sync with finance).

Attachments: privnet-heartbeat-logs-20280514.zip, controlplane-config-diff-20280514.txt

— Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medicor.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Private sync gap (v2.3.1)

Sanjay —

Thanks again for the bridge yesterday. Below is a concise post-incident summary, timeline, and proposed customer-facing mitigations. I’ve attached a short postmortem PDF with the full timeline for your records.

Summary (TL;DR):
- During the scheduled v2.3.1 upgrade in your staging VPC on 2028-05-14 09:10 PT, a combination of a reconciler timing regression and a customer cluster heartbeat parameter set to 1.5s caused ~12 agents to briefly drop heartbeats and trigger leader reassignments. Traffic degraded (503s) intermittently for ~2 seconds. No data loss detected.

Timeline (high level):
- 09:10 PT — upgrade window begins.
- 09:11:53 PT — leader handoff sequence observed in control plane logs.
- 09:11:58–09:12:02 PT — agent heartbeats missed; short 503 spike observed.
- 09:13 PT — temporary config toggle applied; traffic recovered.

Customer impact: brief latency/regressions for a small percentage of requests. No PII or persistent state corruption.

Permanent fixes we are implementing:
- Code: guarded fix to reconciler to avoid aggressive leader handoffs during rolling upgrades (targeted release: 2028-05-22).
- Policy: update recommended heartbeat baseline and add an automated pre-upgrade validator that flags heartbeat windows below 3s.
- Runbook: add a section to the private-runbook (linked) for quick rollback and temporary heartbeat widening.

Compensation / credits:
- We are prepared to discuss a goodwill operational credit for the upgrade window; Ben is evaluating and will confirm by EOD tomorrow.

Artifacts and evidence:
- Attached: postmortem-timeline-20280516.pdf, heartbeat logs, config diff.
- JIRA: JIRA-PRIV-4567 (contains raw logs and traces).
- Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPrivNetRunbook

Requested customer action:
- Please confirm if you would like us to schedule the guarded v2.3.1 re-deploy in staging next week (we recommend running the canary with the fix first).

If you prefer, we can also run a joint verification window prior to any production upgrades.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll keep you updated as the guarded fix lands and we finish the runbook updates.

Best —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-timeline-20280516.pdf

Sanjay —

Thanks for your patience while we validated the initial remediation plan. I’m authorizing an operational credit conversation with finance; we’ll quantify exposure and follow up tomorrow with specifics.

High-level on our commitment:
- We will ship the guarded reconciler fix on 2028-05-22 and schedule a canary re-deploy in staging.
- We will provide a pre-upgrade validator check as part of our Private upgrade checklist so this configuration mismatch cannot silently recur.

If that plan sounds acceptable, Grace or Tessa will reach out to book the canary window and coordinate timelines.

— Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
